entries.text: a
entries.script: Say "aaa" — the sound in apple, ant, cat.

how.avoid: Not 'ay' — that's the letter's name.

entries.text: m
entries.script: Say "mmmmm" — the sound in moon, man, mud.

how.avoid: Lips together and hum. No 'muh'.

entries.text: s

how.avoid: A long hiss. No 'suh'.

entries.text: t

entries.text: h

entries.text: b

entries.text: j

entries.text: w

how.avoid: Round your lips. As short as you can, not 'wuh'.

entries.script: Say "k" — the sound in duck, pack, sick.

how.avoid: Two letters, one sound, always at the end. NOT 'kuh'.

entries.text: ch

how.avoid: Like a train starting. NOT 'chuh'.

entries.script: The word "wind", said clearly and slowly.

entries.text: wing
entries.script: The word "wing", said clearly and slowly.

entries.text: wink
entries.script: The word "wink", said clearly and slowly.

entries.text: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again."

entries.text: One from each of the last few days.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One from each of the last few days."

entries.text: Same start, same ending. Listen hard to the middle.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Same start, same ending. Listen hard to the middle."

entries.text: One of these has an extra sound at the front. Listen before the vowel.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One of these has an extra sound at the front. Listen before the vowel."

entries.text: A blend on the front and a blend on the back.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A blend on the front and a blend on the back."

entries.text: This pair is not like sh or ch. Here you really do hear both letters — they are just in a hurry.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "This pair is not like sh or ch. Here you really do hear both letters — they are just in a hurry."

entries.text: Two of these are half of the third. Find the one that is both.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Two of these are half of the third. Find the one that is both."

entries.text: Two letters, two sounds, said in a hurry. No little vowel in the middle.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Two letters, two sounds, said in a hurry. No little vowel in the middle."

entries.text: Only the first sound has changed. Keep the ending exactly the same.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Only the first sound has changed. Keep the ending exactly the same."

entries.text: Same again. The word is longer than it sounds.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Same again. The word is longer than it sounds."

entries.text: Same three letters at the front. One of them has the silent e on the end.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Same three letters at the front. One of them has the silent e on the end."

entries.text: Only the middle has changed. Keep the front exactly the same.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Only the middle has changed. Keep the front exactly the same."

entries.text: The new blend goes first. Slide the two sounds together before you say the rest.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "The new blend goes first. Slide the two sounds together before you say the rest."

entries.text: All three start the same. The last sound decides it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start the same. The last sound decides it."

entries.text: Four sounds. Do not let the t slip off the end.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds. Do not let the t slip off the end."

entries.text: One of these stops with a little tap on the end. Find the one with the tap.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One of these stops with a little tap on the end. Find the one with the tap."

entries.text: Only the first sound has changed.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Only the first sound has changed."

entries.text: Same again. Only the vowel moved.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Same again. Only the vowel moved."

entries.text: Same ending. Only the first sound is different.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Same ending. Only the first sound is different."

entries.text: Two of these are one sound on its own. Find the pair.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Two of these are one sound on its own. Find the pair."

entries.text: A new one today. It says…
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A new one today. It says…"

entries.text: A team at the front and the new blend at the back.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A team at the front and the new blend at the back."

entries.text: All three end the same way. This time the clue is in the middle.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three end the same way. This time the clue is in the middle."

entries.text: All three have a gap and a quiet e. Listen to the vowel that goes in the gap.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three have a gap and a quiet e. Listen to the vowel that goes in the gap."

entries.text: All three have a k in them. Find the one that starts with a hiss.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three have a k in them. Find the one that starts with a hiss."

entries.text: All three start the same way. This time the clue is at the end.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start the same way. This time the clue is at the end."

entries.text: Hiss the s with your teeth almost shut, then hump the back of your tongue up and pop it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hiss the s with your teeth almost shut, then hump the back of your tongue up and pop it."

entries.text: Hiss the s with your teeth almost shut, then tap your tongue down for the t.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hiss the s with your teeth almost shut, then tap your tongue down for the t."

entries.text: Only the middle sound is new. The rest you have known for weeks.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Only the middle sound is new. The rest you have known for weeks."

entries.text: Same ending, with a round mouth in the middle.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Same ending, with a round mouth in the middle."

entries.text: Say the hiss and the pop on their own first, then push them together.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Say the hiss and the pop on their own first, then push them together."

entries.text: The new blend at the front and a team at the back.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "The new blend at the front and a team at the back."

entries.text: The same sound as today, spelled the other way.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "The same sound as today, spelled the other way."

entries.text: The same two letters, back where you met them.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "The same two letters, back where you met them."

entries.text: These all end with an r. Listen to the very first sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "These all end with an r. Listen to the very first sound."

entries.text: Three hisses. This one ends with a pop at the back of your mouth.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Three hisses. This one ends with a pop at the back of your mouth."

entries.text: Three sounds, not four. The m and the e go together and the e stays quiet.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Three sounds, not four. The m and the e go together and the e stays quiet."

entries.text: Two l letters on the end, but only one sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Two l letters on the end, but only one sound."

entries.text: Two of these work on their own. One is a team of two letters saying one sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Two of these work on their own. One is a team of two letters saying one sound."

entries.text: Two sounds at the front this time, and the quiet e still at the back.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Two sounds at the front this time, and the quiet e still at the back."

entries.text: Two sounds at the front, and the quiet e still at the back.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Two sounds at the front, and the quiet e still at the back."

entries.text: A big S at the front. Big S and small s say the same sound — names get the big one.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A big S at the front. Big S and small s say the same sound — names get the big one."

entries.text: A blend at each end of this one. Sound it out slowly first.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A blend at each end of this one. Sound it out slowly first."

entries.text: A blend on the end. Keep the m and the p in one piece.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A blend on the end. Keep the m and the p in one piece."

entries.text: A blend on the front and a team in the middle.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A blend on the front and a team in the middle."

entries.text: A brand new vowel. Its name is oh, but the sound it makes is o.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A brand new vowel. Its name is oh, but the sound it makes is o."

entries.text: A buzz at each end and /a/ in the middle.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A buzz at each end and /a/ in the middle." Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: A cab is a taxi. Back pop, front pop.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A cab is a taxi. Back pop, front pop."

entries.text: A clam shuts itself up inside two shells.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A clam shuts itself up inside two shells."

entries.text: A daft dog is a silly one.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A daft dog is a silly one."

entries.text: A dim room is one where the light is nearly out.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A dim room is one where the light is nearly out."

entries.text: A doe is a deer with no antlers on her head.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A doe is a deer with no antlers on her head."

entries.text: A duck has a bill. So does a letter that comes asking for money.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A duck has a bill. So does a letter that comes asking for money."

entries.text: A fig is a small sweet fruit, full of tiny seeds.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A fig is a small sweet fruit, full of tiny seeds."

entries.text: A flock is a big bunch of sheep or birds.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A flock is a big bunch of sheep or birds."

entries.text: A frock is a dress. The ck at the back is one quick pop.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A frock is a dress. The ck at the back is one quick pop."

entries.text: A gap is a hole where something is missing — like a lost tooth.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A gap is a hole where something is missing — like a lost tooth."

entries.text: A hint is a small clue. Four sounds again, with the /n/ hiding in the middle.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A hint is a small clue. Four sounds again, with the /n/ hiding in the middle." Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: A hiss and a pop, squashed together at the front. Say them both: /s/, /k/.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A hiss and a pop, squashed together at the front. Say them both: /s/, /k/." Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: A hiss, then the round lips. Four sounds — do not let the /w/ get lost.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A hiss, then the round lips. Four sounds — do not let the /w/ get lost." Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: A hoe digs up the mud in a garden.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A hoe digs up the mud in a garden."

entries.text: A jab is a quick little poke. Only the last sound has changed.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A jab is a quick little poke. Only the last sound has changed."

entries.text: A jig is a bouncy dance. Small vowel this time.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A jig is a bouncy dance. Small vowel this time."

entries.text: A long hiss, then a small vowel, then stop.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A long hiss, then a small vowel, then stop."

entries.text: A long one with two vowels in it. The first one is short and the second one says its name.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A long one with two vowels in it. The first one is short and the second one says its name."

entries.text: A long one. Read dig, then add ing on the back: dig — ing.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A long one. Read dig, then add ing on the back: dig — ing."

entries.text: A long one. The o is short at the front and the team says oh at the end.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A long one. The o is short at the front and the team says oh at the end."

entries.text: A name this time. It ends with lips shut and humming.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A name this time. It ends with lips shut and humming."

entries.text: A name, and it works just like the others.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A name, and it works just like the others."

entries.text: A new vowel in the middle and the new blend at the end.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A new vowel in the middle and the new blend at the end."

entries.text: A pop at the front and a pop at the end. Same letter both times.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A pop at the front and a pop at the end. Same letter both times."

entries.text: A question again. Let your voice lift at the end.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A question again. Let your voice lift at the end."

entries.text: A quiet e on the end, so the i says its name in the middle.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A quiet e on the end, so the i says its name in the middle."

entries.text: A small word you will use in nearly every sentence from now on.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A small word you will use in nearly every sentence from now on."

entries.text: A snag is a bit that gets stuck.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A snag is a bit that gets stuck."

entries.text: A swig is one big gulp of a drink.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A swig is one big gulp of a drink."

entries.text: A team at the front and a blend at the back.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A team at the front and a blend at the back."

entries.text: A team at the front and the new vowel behind it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A team at the front and the new vowel behind it."

entries.text: A theme is a tune that comes back. Two letters at the front, one sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A theme is a tune that comes back. Two letters at the front, one sound."

entries.text: A vat is a huge tub. Only the last sound has changed.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A vat is a huge tub. Only the last sound has changed."

entries.text: Again, and a bit faster. It is somebody's name.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Again, and a bit faster. It is somebody's name."

entries.text: All five vowels, all with a silent e on the end. Still saying their own names.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All five vowels, all with a silent e on the end. Still saying their own names."

entries.text: All of these you can still sound out. Only the is different.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All of these you can still sound out. Only the is different."

entries.text: All of these you have read before. One more time, left to right.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All of these you have read before. One more time, left to right."

entries.text: All three are built out of a, and all three say something different.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three are built out of a, and all three say something different."

entries.text: All three are made of air. Find /fff/.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three are made of air. Find /fff/." Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: All three are made of e. One of them has a gap with a letter hiding in it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three are made of e. One of them has a gap with a letter hiding in it."

entries.text: All three are made with your lips. Find the one that pushes air forward.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three are made with your lips. Find the one that pushes air forward."

entries.text: All three are quick taps. Find /t/.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three are quick taps. Find /t/." Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: All three are two letters with one sound. Listen for the little puff.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three are two letters with one sound. Listen for the little puff."

entries.text: All three end the same way. The blend at the front decides it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three end the same way. The blend at the front decides it."

entries.text: All three end the same way. This time the clue is at the front.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three end the same way. This time the clue is at the front."

entries.text: All three end with an l. Which one starts with a pop at your lips?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three end with an l. Which one starts with a pop at your lips?"

entries.text: All three end with your lips. Find the one that starts with a hiss.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three end with your lips. Find the one that starts with a hiss."

entries.text: All three have a gap and a silent e. Listen to the vowel that goes in the gap.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three have a gap and a silent e. Listen to the vowel that goes in the gap."

entries.text: All three put your tongue in the same spot. Find the one that keeps humming.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three put your tongue in the same spot. Find the one that keeps humming."

entries.text: All three start alike. Hold on to the very last sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start alike. Hold on to the very last sound."

entries.text: All three start at the back of your mouth. Find the one where your tongue pulls back.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start at the back of your mouth. Find the one where your tongue pulls back."

entries.text: All three start the same way at the back of your mouth. This one ends with a pop.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start the same way at the back of your mouth. This one ends with a pop."

entries.text: All three start the same way. The last sound decides it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start the same way. The last sound decides it."

entries.text: All three start the same. Everything depends on the last sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start the same. Everything depends on the last sound."

entries.text: All three start with dr. The middle sound decides it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start with dr. The middle sound decides it."

entries.text: All three start with g. The middle sound decides it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start with g. The middle sound decides it."

entries.text: All three start with h and an e. The end of the word decides it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start with h and an e. The end of the word decides it."

entries.text: All three start with the pop. The last sound is the one to listen for.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start with the pop. The last sound is the one to listen for."

entries.text: All three start with the same hiss. This time the clue is at the end.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start with the same hiss. This time the clue is at the end."

entries.text: All three start with the same pop. Everything hangs on the last sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start with the same pop. Everything hangs on the last sound."

entries.text: All three start with tr. The middle sound decides it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start with tr. The middle sound decides it."

entries.text: All three start with tr. The sound after it decides which one you heard.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start with tr. The sound after it decides which one you heard."

entries.text: All three start with your lips. Find the one where your tongue pulls back.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start with your lips. Find the one where your tongue pulls back."

entries.text: All three vowels you know. Listen for the one with the jaw right down.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three vowels you know. Listen for the one with the jaw right down."

entries.text: And dr in one piece. Three sounds: dr, i, p.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "And dr in one piece. Three sounds: dr, i, p."

entries.text: And the quick tap?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "And the quick tap?"

entries.text: And the wide-open one. Where is /a/?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "And the wide-open one. Where is /a/?" Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: Another noisy twin. Shut your lips, then let them go.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Another noisy twin. Shut your lips, then let them go."

entries.text: Another one you can hold. It says…
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Another one you can hold. It says…"

entries.text: Another pair of letters sharing one sound. This one is short and sharp, like a little train.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Another pair of letters sharing one sound. This one is short and sharp, like a little train."

entries.text: Another team of two letters. They do not say o and then e. Together they say oh.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Another team of two letters. They do not say o and then e. Together they say oh."

entries.text: Another team of two letters. They do not say u and then e. Together they say oo.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Another team of two letters. They do not say u and then e. Together they say oo."

entries.text: At the end of a short word, l likes to bring a friend along. They still only say it once.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "At the end of a short word, l likes to bring a friend along. They still only say it once."

entries.text: Back to the end of the word. Same two sounds, other spelling.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Back to the end of the word. Same two sounds, other spelling."

entries.text: Back to words we can sound out. Two teams, three sounds.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Back to words we can sound out. Two teams, three sounds."

entries.text: Big J, small a, small ck. Only the first letter is wearing its big coat.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Big J, small a, small ck. Only the first letter is wearing its big coat."

entries.text: Blends at the front. Today's new bit was in the middle.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Blends at the front. Today's new bit was in the middle."

entries.text: Both are made at the back. Hand on your throat — which one buzzes?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both are made at the back. Hand on your throat — which one buzzes?"

entries.text: Both are quick and both buzz. One is at the back of your mouth — that one is /g/.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both are quick and both buzz. One is at the back of your mouth — that one is /g/." Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: Both are real words. The middle sound is the only difference — listen for the small one.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both are real words. The middle sound is the only difference — listen for the small one."

entries.text: Both end the same way. Is there a buzz at the front or not?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both end the same way. Is there a buzz at the front or not?"

entries.text: Both end with a hiss and a pop. Which pop is it?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both end with a hiss and a pop. Which pop is it?"

entries.text: Both happen at the back of your mouth. Hand on your throat: one buzzes and one does not.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both happen at the back of your mouth. Hand on your throat: one buzzes and one does not."

entries.text: Both of these are just air. For /f/ you squeeze it past your teeth; for /h/ nothing gets in the way.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both of these are just air. For /f/ you squeeze it past your teeth; for /h/ nothing gets in the way." Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: Both of these are made of the same three sounds. Start at the left.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both of these are made of the same three sounds. Start at the left."

entries.text: Both of these come down your nose. /m/ has your lips shut; for /n/ they stay open. Which is /n/?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both of these come down your nose. /m/ has your lips shut; for /n/ they stay open. Which is /n/?" Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: Both of these start with your lips shut. One hums, one pops. Find the pop.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both of these start with your lips shut. One hums, one pops. Find the pop."

entries.text: Both say the o sound. One has a team of two letters and one has a silent e on the end.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both say the o sound. One has a team of two letters and one has a silent e on the end."

entries.text: Both start at the back of your mouth. Hand on your throat: which one buzzes?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both start at the back of your mouth. Hand on your throat: which one buzzes?"

entries.text: Both start the same. Does it end at the back of your mouth or at your teeth?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both start the same. Does it end at the back of your mouth or at your teeth?"

entries.text: Both start with a b. Does the tongue flick up to the teeth, or pull back?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both start with a b. Does the tongue flick up to the teeth, or pull back?"

entries.text: Both start with a c. Does the tongue pull back, or flick up to the teeth?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both start with a c. Does the tongue pull back, or flick up to the teeth?"

entries.text: Both start with a hiss. Is the next sound a pop from your lips or a tap from your tongue?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both start with a hiss. Is the next sound a pop from your lips or a tap from your tongue?"

entries.text: Both start with an f. Listen hard to the sound just after it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both start with an f. Listen hard to the sound just after it."

entries.text: Both start with bl. Listen right to the end: a pop from your lips or a tap from your tongue?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both start with bl. Listen right to the end: a pop from your lips or a tap from your tongue?"

entries.text: Both start with sk. Listen right to the end: an n or an m?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both start with sk. Listen right to the end: an n or an m?"

entries.text: Both start with t. The team in the middle is the only thing that changes.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both start with t. The team in the middle is the only thing that changes."

entries.text: Buzz or no buzz? That is the only difference.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Buzz or no buzz? That is the only difference."

entries.text: Buzz, wide vowel, hum.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Buzz, wide vowel, hum."

entries.text: Careful — both of these sounds live in your nose. Keep them separate.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Careful — both of these sounds live in your nose. Keep them separate."

entries.text: Check the end and the middle on this one.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Check the end and the middle on this one."

entries.text: Do not sound this one out. It is a word we just know by sight: is.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Do not sound this one out. It is a word we just know by sight: is."

entries.text: Do not sound this one out. It is a word we just know by sight: the.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Do not sound this one out. It is a word we just know by sight: the."

entries.text: Do not sound this one out. It is a word we just know by sight: they.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Do not sound this one out. It is a word we just know by sight: they."

entries.text: Does the start stop quickly, or go on and on?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Does the start stop quickly, or go on and on?"

entries.text: Does the tongue touch behind your teeth, or does it stay back?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Does the tongue touch behind your teeth, or does it stay back?"

entries.text: Eight words — the longest yet. Read the first half, then the second.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Eight words — the longest yet. Read the first half, then the second."

entries.text: Every one of these has the everyday a. Tomorrow you will see what a silent e does to it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Every one of these has the everyday a. Tomorrow you will see what a silent e does to it."

entries.text: Every one of these turns into a silent e word if you stick an e on it. Try it out loud.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Every one of these turns into a silent e word if you stick an e on it. Try it out loud."

entries.text: Every other sound needs your lips or your tongue. This one needs only your breath.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Every other sound needs your lips or your tongue. This one needs only your breath."

entries.text: Every sound so far has been at the front of your mouth. This one lives at the back.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Every sound so far has been at the front of your mouth. This one lives at the back."

entries.text: Exactly the same back-of-the-tongue pop as c and k. Two letters on the page, one job for your mouth.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Exactly the same back-of-the-tongue pop as c and k. Two letters on the page, one job for your mouth."

entries.text: Exactly the same mouth as sc. The hiss, then the pop at the back.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Exactly the same mouth as sc. The hiss, then the pop at the back."

entries.text: Exactly the same mouth for both. Only one of them tickles your lip.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Exactly the same mouth for both. Only one of them tickles your lip."

entries.text: Exactly the same tongue, exactly the same hum. Two letters, one sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Exactly the same tongue, exactly the same hum. Two letters, one sound."

entries.text: Find it again.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Find it again."

entries.text: Find the one with a gap in the middle. A letter goes in that gap.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Find the one with a gap in the middle. A letter goes in that gap."

entries.text: Find the two letters that share one pop.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Find the two letters that share one pop."

entries.text: Finger under the word. Off you go.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Finger under the word. Off you go."

entries.text: Five days, five words. Read them all the way through.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Five days, five words. Read them all the way through."

entries.text: Five sounds, the longest word yet. Take them one at a time and don't drop the /n/.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Five sounds, the longest word yet. Take them one at a time and don't drop the /n/." Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: Five sounds. The last two are both made with your lips — don't let them squash into one.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Five sounds. The last two are both made with your lips — don't let them squash into one."

entries.text: Four days, two vowels, one trick: the vowel says its own name.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four days, two vowels, one trick: the vowel says its own name."

entries.text: Four sounds and no letter teams. Take them one at a time.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds and no letter teams. Take them one at a time."

entries.text: Four sounds now. Do not let the d slip off the end.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds now. Do not let the d slip off the end."

entries.text: Four sounds so far. Which one is /a/?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds so far. Which one is /a/?" Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: Four sounds this time. Daft is another word for silly.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds this time. Daft is another word for silly."

entries.text: Four sounds — the tall pole on a boat. Take it slowly.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds — the tall pole on a boat. Take it slowly."

entries.text: Four sounds, and the first two run straight into each other: sss-nnn-a-p.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds, and the first two run straight into each other: sss-nnn-a-p."

entries.text: Four sounds, and the last two are close together. Slowly.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds, and the last two are close together. Slowly."

entries.text: Four sounds, and the last two are squashed close together. Go slowly.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds, and the last two are squashed close together. Go slowly."

entries.text: Four sounds. A stag is a deer with big antlers.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds. A stag is a deer with big antlers."

entries.text: Four sounds. Do not let the p slip off the end.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds. Do not let the p slip off the end."

entries.text: Four sounds. Slowly, even though it says fast.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds. Slowly, even though it says fast."

entries.text: Four sounds. The /n/ is quick and easy to lose — go slowly.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds. The /n/ is quick and easy to lose — go slowly." Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: Four sounds. The /n/ is quick and easy to skip — say it anyway.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds. The /n/ is quick and easy to skip — say it anyway." Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: Four sounds. The hum in the middle is easy to lose.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds. The hum in the middle is easy to lose."

entries.text: Four sounds: s, then l, then the team, then p.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds: s, then l, then the team, then p."

entries.text: Four vowels you have had for weeks. The fifth one is new.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four vowels you have had for weeks. The fifth one is new."

entries.text: Four vowels, one quiet e, one job. Today's e was the last of the set.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four vowels, one quiet e, one job. Today's e was the last of the set."

entries.text: Four words in a row — this is new. Point at the first one and read only that one.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four words in a row — this is new. Point at the first one and read only that one."

entries.text: Four words with a gap and a quiet e. Listen to the vowel that goes in the gap.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four words with a gap and a quiet e. Listen to the vowel that goes in the gap."

entries.text: Grin has two sounds before the vowel. Say them both.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Grin has two sounds before the vowel. Say them both."

entries.text: Here is our second vowel. Every word you know has a vowel hiding in the middle of it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Here is our second vowel. Every word you know has a vowel hiding in the middle of it."

entries.text: Here it is again. What does it say?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Here it is again. What does it say?"

entries.text: Hiss the s with your teeth almost shut, then push your lips into a tight round for the w.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hiss the s with your teeth almost shut, then push your lips into a tight round for the w."

entries.text: Hiss the s with your teeth almost shut, then shut your lips and pop them open for the p.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hiss the s with your teeth almost shut, then shut your lips and pop them open for the p."

entries.text: Hiss the s, then hum the n without moving your tongue. It stays behind your top teeth the whole time.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hiss the s, then hum the n without moving your tongue. It stays behind your top teeth the whole time."

entries.text: Hold the f for a long time, then tap the t: sooooff-t.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hold the f for a long time, then tap the t: sooooff-t."

entries.text: Hold the first sound as long as you like, then keep going.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hold the first sound as long as you like, then keep going."

entries.text: Hold the first sound, then tap the second. Aaa-t.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hold the first sound, then tap the second. Aaa-t."

entries.text: Hold the hiss, then finish at the back. A bag full of rocks makes a shelf sag.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hold the hiss, then finish at the back. A bag full of rocks makes a shelf sag."

entries.text: Hold the hiss, then finish with a buzz.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hold the hiss, then finish with a buzz."

entries.text: Hold the n for a long time, then tap the d: sannnn-d.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hold the n for a long time, then tap the d: sannnn-d."

entries.text: Hold the s for a long time, then tap the t: misssss-t.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hold the s for a long time, then tap the t: misssss-t."

entries.text: Hum or pop at the end? Listen right to the last sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hum or pop at the end? Listen right to the last sound."

entries.text: Hum the m for a long time, then pop the p: dammmm-p.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hum the m for a long time, then pop the p: dammmm-p."

entries.text: Hum, small vowel, buzz.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hum, small vowel, buzz."

entries.text: Hum, tap or buzz? Listen to the last sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hum, tap or buzz? Listen to the last sound."

entries.text: Hump the back of your tongue up and pop it for the c, then flick the tip up behind your teeth for the l.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hump the back of your tongue up and pop it for the c, then flick the tip up behind your teeth for the l."

entries.text: Hump the back of your tongue up and pop it for the c, then pull the tongue back for the r.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hump the back of your tongue up and pop it for the c, then pull the tongue back for the r."

entries.text: In all of these the tongue flicks up. In today's words it pulls back.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "In all of these the tongue flicks up. In today's words it pulls back."

entries.text: Jill is a name. Two l's at the end, said once.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Jill is a name. Two l's at the end, said once."

entries.text: Just a puff of warm air out of your throat — like fogging up a cold window. Your mouth does nothing.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Just a puff of warm air out of your throat — like fogging up a cold window. Your mouth does nothing."

entries.text: Just two sounds to start with. The vowel goes first this time.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Just two sounds to start with. The vowel goes first this time."

entries.text: Keep the ue in one piece in the middle and add the s at the end.

entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last hunt. Where is /m/?" Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: Last hunt. Where is the tap?

entries.text: Last hunt. Which one buzzes against your lip?

entries.text: Last one. Where is /a/?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last one. Where is /a/?" Where it says something like /a/, say the SOUND itself, not "slash a slash".

entries.text: Lips forward in a tiny circle, like blowing out a candle. Nothing touches — no teeth, no tongue.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Lips forward in a tiny circle, like blowing out a candle. Nothing touches — no teeth, no tongue."

entries.text: Lips pushed forward in a small circle, held steady: ooo. The same shape as blue.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Lips pushed forward in a small circle, held steady: ooo. The same shape as blue."

entries.text: Lips pushed forward into a round o — the same shape as yesterday, held a little longer.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Lips pushed forward into a round o — the same shape as yesterday, held a little longer."

entries.text: Lips shut tight, then pop them open — with your voice on. Hand on your throat: /b/ buzzes, /p/ does not.

entries.text: Lips wide in a smile, teeth almost shut: eee. The same sound as yesterday's bee.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Lips wide in a smile, teeth almost shut: eee. The same sound as yesterday's bee."

entries.text: Lips, tongue tap, or buzz at the end?

entries.text: Listen carefully. Which one is it?

entries.text: Listen to which sound comes first.

entries.text: Long words, and only the last two sounds are different. Listen right to the end.

entries.text: No new sound today, so these are all words you can already sound out.
